_about: Thematic structure of the Bhagavad Gita used for indexing. Chapter summaries, section titles and theme descriptions are original to this project. Sections are the PARENT chunks of the parent-child RAG index; each verse (shloka) is a CHILD chunk.

hexads.title: Hexad I - The Path of Action (Karma)
hexads.summary: From Arjuna's collapse on the battlefield to the discipline of selfless action and meditation: who we are (the immortal Self) and how to act without bondage.

hexads.title: Hexad II - The Path of Devotion (Bhakti)
hexads.summary: Krishna reveals his own nature: the source of all beings, the royal secret, his divine glories and the cosmic form, culminating in loving devotion as the most direct way.

hexads.title: Hexad III - The Path of Knowledge (Jnana)
hexads.summary: Analysis of matter and spirit, the three gunas, divine and demonic natures, faith, and finally the synthesis of renunciation, duty and surrender that ends Arjuna's doubt.

themes.name: Battlefield narrative
themes.description: The frame story at Kurukshetra: the armies, the warriors, conches blowing, Sanjaya reporting to Dhritarashtra.

themes.name: Arjuna's grief and moral crisis
themes.description: Arjuna's despair, compassion for kinsmen, fear of sin and refusal to fight; confusion about duty.

themes.name: The immortal Self (Atman)
themes.description: The soul is eternal, unborn and indestructible; bodies change like garments; do not grieve for what cannot die.

themes.name: Duty and one's own dharma
themes.description: Performing one's own duty according to one's nature and station; better one's own duty imperfectly done than another's well done.

themes.name: Selfless action (Karma Yoga)
themes.description: Acting without attachment to the fruits of action; work as an offering; action, inaction and wise action.

themes.name: Equanimity and the steady mind
themes.description: The person of steady wisdom, even-minded in pleasure and pain, success and failure, praise and blame; inner peace.

themes.name: Mind, senses, desire and anger
themes.description: Controlling the restless mind and the senses; desire and anger as the enemy; the chain from attachment to ruin.

themes.name: Sacrifice (Yajna) and offering
themes.description: Sacrifice as cosmic reciprocity; many forms of sacrifice; offering every act, food and gift to the divine.

themes.name: Knowledge and wisdom (Jnana)
themes.description: Spiritual knowledge that burns away karma; learning from the wise; discrimination between the real and unreal.

themes.name: Meditation and self-discipline (Dhyana)
themes.description: How to sit and meditate, moderation in food and sleep, steadying the mind like a lamp in a windless place.

themes.name: Devotion and surrender (Bhakti)
themes.description: Loving devotion to God, offering a leaf or flower with love, taking refuge, surrender, the qualities of a dear devotee.

themes.name: Krishna's divine nature and glories
themes.description: Krishna as the source and essence of all, his incarnations to restore righteousness, his higher and lower nature, his divine manifestations (vibhutis).

themes.name: The Universal Form (Vishvarupa)
themes.description: Arjuna's vision of the cosmic form of God with countless faces, blazing like a thousand suns, as all-devouring Time.

themes.name: Creation, death and rebirth
themes.description: Brahman, the cycles of creation and dissolution, days and nights of Brahma, remembering God at death, the paths of departure and rebirth.

themes.name: The three Gunas
themes.description: Sattva (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (inertia/darkness): how the qualities of nature bind, and how to transcend them.

themes.name: Field and knower; Prakriti and Purusha
themes.description: The body as the field, the Self as its knower; matter and spirit; the virtues that constitute knowledge; the imperishable Supreme Person.

themes.name: Divine and demonic qualities
themes.description: Fearlessness, purity, compassion versus hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, cruelty; lust, anger and greed as three gates to hell.

themes.name: Faith, food, austerity and charity
themes.description: Three kinds of faith, food, sacrifice, austerity and gifts according to the gunas; Om Tat Sat.

themes.name: Renunciation and liberation (Moksha)
themes.description: Sannyasa and tyaga, renouncing the fruits rather than action, the supreme secret of surrender, attainment of Brahman and freedom.

chapters.summary: The armies face each other at Kurukshetra. Duryodhana reviews the warriors, conches sound, and Arjuna asks Krishna to place the chariot between the armies. Seeing teachers, grandfathers and cousins ready to die, Arjuna is overwhelmed by grief and drops his bow.

Arjuna becomes Krishna's disciple. Krishna teaches the immortality of the Self, the warrior's duty, the discipline of action without attachment to results (2.47), and describes the person of steady wisdom whose mind is unmoved by pleasure and pain.

No one can remain without acting. Action done as sacrifice does not bind; the wise act to keep the world in order and set an example. Better one's own duty than another's. Desire and anger, born of rajas, are the real enemy.

chapters.name_english: Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
chapters.summary: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this yoga and why he incarnates age after age (4.7-8). He explains action, inaction and wise action, lists many forms of sacrifice, and praises knowledge as the fire that burns all karma.

Renunciation and selfless action lead to the same goal, but action is easier. The yogi acts untouched like a lotus leaf on water, sees all beings with an equal eye, and finds joy within, reaching the peace of Brahman.

Raise yourself by yourself; the mind is friend or enemy. Practical instructions for meditation, moderation in eating and sleeping, the restless mind tamed by practice and detachment, and the reassurance that no sincere seeker is ever lost.

Krishna describes his lower eightfold nature and higher conscious nature; he is the taste in water and the light of sun and moon. His maya of the gunas is hard to cross; four kinds of people worship him, and the wise one is dearest.

Definitions of Brahman, adhyatma and karma. Whatever one remembers at death, one attains; so remember Krishna always. The cosmic days and nights of Brahma, and the two paths by which the departed do or do not return.

chapters.name_english: The Royal Knowledge and Royal Secret
chapters.summary: All beings rest in Krishna, yet he is beyond them. He is the father, mother, goal and refuge of the world. He accepts even a leaf, a flower, fruit or water offered with love, and devotion is open to everyone.

Krishna is the source of all; his devotees enjoy his presence and he gives them understanding. At Arjuna's request he names his chief manifestations - among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga - and says all glory is a spark of his splendour.

chapters.name_english: The Vision of the Cosmic Form
chapters.summary: Given divine sight, Arjuna sees the universal form, radiant as a thousand suns, devouring the warriors. Krishna declares himself Time, the destroyer, and asks Arjuna to be his instrument. Terrified, Arjuna praises him and asks to see his gentle form again.

Devotion to the personal God is easier than meditation on the unmanifest. Krishna offers a ladder of practices and lists the qualities of the devotee dear to him: free from hatred, friendly, compassionate, even-minded and content.

The body is the field and the Self its knower. Humility, non-violence and other virtues are true knowledge. The supreme Brahman pervades all, and liberation comes from discerning Prakriti (matter) from Purusha (spirit).

Krishna is the seed-giving father of all beings. Sattva binds by attachment to happiness, rajas by attachment to action, tamas by delusion. One who goes beyond the three gunas through devotion attains immortality.

The world is an inverted ashvattha tree to be cut with detachment. A fragment of Krishna becomes the individual soul. He is the light in sun and fire and the digestive fire in beings - the Supreme Person beyond the perishable and imperishable.

Divine qualities lead to liberation, demonic ones to bondage. The demonic deny truth, live for desire and pride, and descend; lust, anger and greed are the triple gate to hell. Let scripture be the guide.
Each person's faith follows their nature. Food, sacrifice, austerity of body, speech and mind, and charity are each sattvic, rajasic or tamasic. Om Tat Sat sanctifies every act.

Renounce the fruits, not the duties. Knowledge, action, the doer, intellect, resolve and happiness are classified by the gunas. Doing one's own duty is worship. The supreme secret: abandon all and take refuge in Krishna (18.66). Arjuna's doubts are gone and he resolves to act.
